# SEO-102: Suppress indexing of pages that render no substantive content

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `indexing` |

| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `MEDIUM` |

## Statement

A route that legitimately returns 200 but has nothing to show - an empty collection, a profile with no entries, a placeholder awaiting content - is excluded from indexing until it holds content.

## Rationale

Pages with no content of their own are treated as thin, and a template that can generate thousands of them turns a single empty state into a large share of what the engine sees of the site.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Have the route decide indexability from the size of the result set it rendered, suppressing the index directive when the set is empty. Where the empty state is permanent rather than temporary, return 404 instead so the URL leaves the index rather than staying as an excluded entry.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Request a route known to have an empty result set and record its status, robots directives, and the amount of unique text in the response.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `HTTP_STATUS`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: There is no published threshold that separates thin from substantive content, so this control identifies pages with no content of their own rather than pages below a measured size.
